newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait cracks down on trade in work permits.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait cracks down on trade in work permits.

text.p: Kuwait's Social Affairs and Labour Ministry has asked the state prosecutor to question about 300 employers suspected of illegally trading in work permits, an official said in remarks published on Wednesday.

"Hamad al-Me'ddadi, the Undersecretary of the Social Affairs and Labour Ministry, has announced that 300 Kuwaitis were sent to the prosecution on charges of trading in residency visas," al-Anba newspaper said.
Kuwait sets a maximum penalty of a 5,000 dinars ($16,500) fine and three years in prison for people convicted of trading in work permits.
Diplomats say some unscrupulous businessmen in Kuwait form "paper" firms to recruit Asian and Arab labourers through agents in their countries, providing visas and promising jobs in return for a fee.
Once the labourers land, they find no job is available and the company that hired them, often on the promise of work as cleaners or other menial tasks, does not exist.
Another group of suspected employers will be sent to the prosecutor on similar charges, the official added.
Many jobseekers end up unemployed, owing big debts to relatives and friends back home who lent them the cost of a work contract, often about $3,000, they say.
Regulations bar foreign workers arriving in the Gulf Arab state for the first time from changing employers before two years of employment.
Migrant workers, mainly from Asia and Arab countries, make up about one million of the oil country's two million population.
